page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-48 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, which contains 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled at 2.0 threads per core. The instance is configured with 48.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This server does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong CPU capabilities, with both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests placing in the top 25% of evaluated hardware. The AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI cryptography extensions, which contribute to its strong performance in PassMark CPU encryption tests. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show average performance, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 3053.47 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds at 111.99 GB/sec.

In application-specific workloads, the instance demonstrates average performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations. However, it exhibits strong text generation speeds during small-model LLM inference, reaching 306.54 tokens per second. Given its high compute-to-memory ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for tasks such as multi-threaded decompression, batch processing, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
